author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A crowd gathered at the Claremont Visitor Center on Friday for a memorial stair climb marking 25 years since the September 11 attacks. Organized by Claremont Parks and Recreation, the event gave participants a route designed to equal 110 stories, the height of each World Trade Center tower.

The group ranged from children as young as 5 to people in their 80s, and some walkers brought dogs. Two firefighters from nearby Weathersfield climbed in full turnout gear. Participants could choose their own distance and pace rather than complete the entire challenge, while the most demanding option called for 20 loops of 110 stairs in gear or a weighted vest.

The event honored the nearly 3,000 people killed in the 2001 attacks, including hundreds of firefighters and other emergency personnel. Fire Chief Jim Chamberlin told the gathering that the community’s continued remembrance a quarter-century later was both humbling and a hopeful reflection of Claremont. The climb combined a demanding physical tribute with an accessible community observance.
dek: Residents of many ages completed routes modeled on the World Trade Center’s 110 stories during the city’s 25th-anniversary remembrance.
headline: Claremont stair climb honors September 11 victims
